Fantastic read. This seems like the sort of well thought out, well spoken complaint the FCC wants to receive so that real action can take place.

As I've mentioned for months now the net neutrality regulations lay out extensive exceptions for "reasonable network management." The was left poorly defined and the FCC, expecting confusion, already stated in the rules that they'll define and judge it on a case by case basis. To a cynical eye this little more than a political influence check. If you've met political "donation" requirements then your network manipulation is "reasonable network management." If you haven't then you owe millions in fines. Predictably enough all the big players that are getting cited for violations are immediately angling towards this "reasonable network management" exception.

Companies like TWC and AT&T absolutely pass that political influence check. So what will happen now? Is this all going to just be paying lip service to complainants, or will the rules actually be enforced?

That's a good point that I haven't seen raised yet. Optimistically, I'd like to believe that provision may actually be used to retain some leeway for smaller ISPs to whom "reasonable network management" would actually be (arguably) necessary or useful, especially in an environment where they're competing against the major ones.
